evidence: In all four frames the pot sits on the large left burner, with the kettle upright directly behind it at the back of the left burner grate. A blue flame is visible at the left edge of that burner in every frame, including 64.0 s (left shoulder view; wrist camera at 59.2-62.4 s). So the kettle is on the stove and the left burner is lit. Neither object is held. From 59.2 to 62.4 s the arm hovers almost motionless at the front-left of the cooktop; at 64.0 s it lowers toward the control knobs again (the wrist camera shows the knobs, with the left knob in a turned position). This is idle motion after the task is done. Caveat: the pot occupies the centre of the lit burner and the kettle is pushed toward the back, so whether the kettle still counts as on the burner is somewhat uncertain; and if the arm now turns the left knob, the burner could go off.
